# WireGuard fixtures

`proton-multiaddress.conf` is the config that broke `qbt-vpn-netns-setup` on the owner's host:
a Proton VPN download, used **as issued**, carrying two addresses and two resolvers.

```
Error: any valid prefix is expected rather than "10.2.0.2/32,2a07:b944::2:2/128".
qbt-vpn-netns-setup.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
```

It is kept byte-for-byte as the provider wrote it, with one exception: `PrivateKey` and
`PublicKey` are throwaway keys generated by `wg genkey` for this file alone and used by nothing.
They are real keys rather than the word `redacted` on purpose -- the check that consumes this
fixture hands it to the real `wg setconf`, whose parser rejects anything that is not 32 bytes of
base64 before it ever looks at `AllowedIPs`, which is the line that check exists to exercise.

Everything else -- the address list, the resolver list, the `0.0.0.0/0, ::/0` route set, the
endpoint, the keepalive, the spacing after each comma -- is what the provider issues. The defect
this fixture pins is a defect in reading what providers actually write, so a tidied-up or
hand-minimised version of it would not have caught the bug and must not replace it.

Consumed by the `wireguard-config-with-many-addresses` check in `nix/modules/flake/checks.nix`.
